tagline: Four lanes around Branson, with ramps to nowhere at one end.
intro: The Highroad starts at a Route 76 interchange northwest of Branson, where a stub of freeway with ghost ramps runs a short way south and stops. From there four lanes head north through wooded hills, curve northeast into Taney County, and turn east past Route 248 to US 65 north of town.

It opened in June 2003 as Route 465. So that Branson could take over its own strip, the state moved Route 76 onto the Highroad, and the 465 signs came down in 2020. The state owns the right of way to carry the road on to US 65 at the other end, and for lack of funding has no plans to build it.

moments.title: Silver Dollar City
moments.text: Out Route 76 to the west, an 1880s-themed park opened in 1960 at Marvel Cave, whose owner William Lynch once cleared the brush for the road from Branson that became Route 76.

moments.title: Chula Vista
moments.text: A 1,302-foot summit on Route 248, named by a settler who had visited Chula Vista, California, which is Spanish for pretty view.
